subject: .gitattributes omission as root cause of host-side CRLF divergence
header_comment: Byte-exact canonical files asserted by committed-blob or raw-byte hash tests. Keep LF working-tree bytes for these exact paths regardless of core.autocrlf, so raw SHA-256 and Git blob identities match the committed canonical content. Exact paths only: no globs, no repository-wide line-ending policy.

contents: # Byte-exact canonical files asserted by committed-blob or raw-byte hash tests.
# Keep LF working-tree bytes for these exact paths regardless of core.autocrlf,
# so raw SHA-256 and Git blob identities match the committed canonical content.
# Exact paths only: no globs, no repository-wide line-ending policy.
before_fix.consequence_on_windows_with_autocrlf_tru: Git converts LF->CRLF on checkout for unlisted text files; Get-FileHash sees 10425 B CRLF bytes -> 7C6D44B8... mismatch vs manifest 85AC... (10231 B LF)

after_fix.commit_to_be: to be assigned at merge (arena branch correction)

why_instrument_qualifies_as_canonical: Its SHA-256 is published in SHA256SUMS.txt and is referenced by the P-1-C/P-1-D procedure as the operator's execution input; byte identity must be reproducible via Get-FileHash on Windows. This matches the .gitattributes header's criterion exactly.
smallest_governance_compliant_correction: Single-line .gitattributes addition — no instrument byte change, no manifest rewrite, no historical evidence deletion. Preserves prior artifact and explains.
